The given equations represent the squared distances between three points \(A(x_1, y_1)\), \(B(x_2, y_2)\), and \(C(x_3, y_3)\):
\[
AB^2 = 9,\quad AC^2 = 16,\quad BC^2 = 25.
\]
Since \(9 + 16 = 25\), the triangle \(ABC\) satisfies \(AB^2 + AC^2 = BC^2\), so it is a right triangle with the right angle at \(A\). The legs are \(AB = 3\) and \(AC = 4\), so the area of the triangle is
\[
\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 3 \cdot 4 = 6.
\]
The absolute value of the determinant \(\begin{vmatrix} x_1 & y_1 & 1 \\ x_2 & y_2 & 1 \\ x_3 & y_3 & 1 \end{vmatrix}\) is twice the area of the triangle, which is \(12\). Therefore, its square is \(12^2 = 144\).

Answer: 144
